answer: Sybil resistance can come from costly registration: each new agent must deposit a physical resource, say a pound of copper, into a bonded escrow before joining the network, so flooding thousands of fake identities becomes economically painful rather than free. A human registrar signs each deposit with a quill on a ledger scanned at audit time, and any agent caught colluding or double-voting forfeits its stake, which gets burned in a furnace down in the canyon facility. Identity then carries real price, and trust scales with skin in the game.
